newsitem.title: FRANCE: Police called to French Socialist's victory bash.
newsitem.headline: Police called to French Socialist's victory bash.

text.p: Riot police were hurriedly summoned to the French Socialists' election victory party in Paris on Sunday after groups of ultra-leftists, illegal immigrants and homeless tried to gate-crash it.
Television showed people trying to shake open the gates of the Franco-Latin America cultural centre where the party was being held with one man trying to scale the main gate.

Demonstrators unfurled several big red banners marked with hammers and sickles -- the flags of ultra-leftist groups -- while others held up placards reading:"Jospin - You've got to keep your promises."
Socialist leader Lionel Jospin, whose party emerged from Sunday's election runoff as the biggest party in parliament, is likely to be called upon on Monday to form the next government.

Television reporters said blows were exchanged when party security men closed the gates as hundreds of people surged forward to enter the building - sympathisers, demonstrators and non-politically motivated guests trying to join the party.
The Socialists said during their campaign they would seek to cancel new laws aimed at curbing illegal immigration, one of France's most sensitive issues.
Critics say Trotskyite militants are highly active inside the main organised movements defending the homeless and illegal immigrants.
